steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Beat butter and brown sugar together until smooth and creamy.
Add 3 to 3 3/4 cups flour; mix well.
Sprinkle board with remaining flour. Knead for 5 minutes, adding enough flour to make a soft dough.
Roll out dough to 1/2-inch thickness. Cut into 3x1-inch strips.
Prick shortbread cookies with a fork and place on ungreased baking sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until edges are golden brown, 20 to 25 minutes. Cool on the baking sheet briefly before removing to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Scottish Shortbread
raw_recipe.description: Shortbread is a classic Scottish cookie that's easy to make with real butter for a crumbly, melt-in-your-mouth texture and irresistible buttery flavor.

review.reviewBody: I have tried many, many shortbread recipes for the past 41 years in my quest for the "perfect" shortbread - and this is it. I didnt' roll it out but made it into bars - I used 1-8x8" cake pan and one pie plate so they'd be nice and thick. It's even husband approved!!! And he's a very tough cookie to please. Thank you so much!!! Now, I just have to find a butterscotch pie like my mother-in-law used to make and I'm done.

Before I made it I read MANY of the reviews. I am also an experienced baker. I added 1 tablespoon of vanilla (we like vanilla) when I creamed the butter and brown sugar. I added1/4 tsp salt in with the flour. I did NOT knead for 5 minutes as I detest gluten that is tightly woven and chewy or tough in my cookies. I simply mixed in about 4 cups of flour until it was mixed and coming off the edge of my mixing bowl in large clumps and then refrigerated the dough for 30 minutes in a bowl. I dusted some wax paper with powdered sugar and rolled it out using powder sugar if it got sticky. I sprinkled with granulated white sugar and put them close together on my baking sheet as they spread very little. I checked the cookies at 15 minutes and they were close. At 18 minutes they had a golden bottom and had slightly firmed to touch and they were done. I cooled them on the pan for 5 minutes, a rack, then put them in a cookie jar 
Soft, melt in your mouth with a delicate butter flavor, slightly sweet.

I love short bread cookies, but certainly not the price stores charge! I've made Linda's recipe twice now and it's soooo easy and delicious. I did incorporate other ideas from the reviews such as adding vanilla and salt and shaping the dough into two logs, wrapped in wax paper and chilling them in the fridge prior to baking. This makes it much easier to cut the logs into uniform 1/2 slices. I also used dark brown sugar. I found the baking time is pretty critical depending on the thickness of the cookies. I put the first set in and baked for 22 min. and the second set and baked for 24 min. The 2 extra min. gave the second batch a better flaky melt in your mouth texture texture. I had tried chef John's recipe and while good, the process of cutting in the cold butter was a bit tedious and time consuming. I took another reviewer's idea and cut the cold un-salted butter into slices, ringed them on a plate, and micro-waved them on defrost just enough to soften them a bit. It makes it easier to incorporate them using a mixer. The second time I made them I decreased the vanilla by 1/2 tsp. and added 1/2 tsp of almond extract and rolled one log over cinnamon sugar prior to slicing and baking. They tasted was so good!

I made these for the Christmas holidays. They went over very well. They freeze well. 
I used, light brown sugar, unsalted butter, used 1/4 c. less flour, spread the dough mixture in the shallow pan, took a pizza cutter and made 1 inch squares, poked each with a fork. After baking I brushed on melted salted butter to give a smooth finish without the floury texture. And sprinkled icing sugar on top. Pure buttery heaven.

This is such an easy and delicious recipe. I used whole grain flour, 3 3/4 cups, and 1 1/2 tsp vanilla extract. I rolled out in powdered sugar and cut into hearts. After cooking and cooling I used an eggless royal icing to finish. My husband loved them!!

I added 1 Tablespoon vanilla extract and 1/2 tsp. salt.
I creamed butter and sugar for 10 min. 
I used the dough hook and kneaded for 7 min.
I formed the dough into two separate rectangles wrapped in plastic wrap and chilled for 20 min., then sliced in 1/2" slices and placed on parchment lined cookie sheets. 25 min. was perfect
I dipped half the cookies in chocolate.
Excellent.

Made twice. Basic recipe is useable and adaptable, which is what recipes should be before you find ways to make them your own. Here were my changes.
1/4ed the recipe. Added 1/8 tsp salt. Added drop of vanilla extract, a drop of almond extract. Formed dough in a long rectangular log and rolled each side in sugar crystals. Wrapped dough and froze it for a couple of hours or so. Took it out for defrosting and looked for forms to make imprints in cookies. Chose an owl form on a teaspoon and shell forms on hors d'oeuvres picks (pictures included). Cut dough squares about a 1/2 inch thick (if the dough breaks as you cut, it needs to defrost more-found that out the hard way!). Dipped forms in flour, tapped out flour, made imprints, pricked along cookie edges with a fork, and baked for about 15-20 minutes, checking for brownness, and adding more time if needed. Let them cool completely before eating: flavor improves. Freezable afterward. Giving as a gift.

THIS SHORTBREAD IS AMAZING!!!! I made this for the annual cookie exchange and everyone has asked for the recipe! I did tweak this a little bit according to other reviews, adding a pinch of salt and 1 tsp of vanilla. I also ran out of brown sugar so had to substitute with white. 4 cups of flour was the perfect amount, I actually thought it was a little crumbly but they didn't break so it all worked out. I rolled it into balls, topped with sugar and then pressed them down with a glass. They were done in 15 minutes and so amazing. Can't wait to make these again!

This shortbread came out perfectly for me. I did add a 1/2 teaspoon of salt and two teaspoons of good vanilla extract. I tried cutting the dough into rectangles but found it very time consuming so I used a small round cookie cutter. Baking time was 18 minutes for mine. They are crispy, light and delicious. Will make this recipe over and over since shortbread is my favorite cookie. Thanks All Recipes!
I always add 1 tbsp (or two) of vanilla, and 1/2 teaspoon of salt (the salt makes it taste JUST LIKE WALKER brand)

These are SO delicious, it left me wondering how they could have possibly gotten a bad review... until I tasted my first tray. I had baked them until they were puffed up and white... but these were much better after they turned just slightly golden. I had made the cookies on subsequent trays thinner, maybe 1/4 - 1/3 of an inch, and baked them 2 minutes longer, until they were golden. I tried these first, and they were beyond delicious. I chilled the dough, then rolled them in half flour, half powdered sugar, as another reviewer very helpfully suggested. I suspect the person who left a very bad review didn't bake them long enough. My underbaked cookies were crumbly and tasted like flour, not butter. Oh, and I chilled them for an hour after kneading, but before rolling and cutting. I baked on parchment paper instead of poking holes to prevent air bubbles. Adding less flour initially made for better cookies.
Very good, I was wondering if I could replace some of the butter with coconut oil, since there is a lot of butter in the recipe. I did add a pinch of salt to add some more flavor.
Very nice, I added mj butter.
Great. Make again a little thinner, a little salt, maybe sugar on top, maybe chill dough before cutting, definitely cook until golden on edges, the more well-done pieces were better.
Followed the recipe completely. This was delicious!

I first made this several years ago due to comments a friend made. He said essentially that tea deserves a good biscuit. He’s originally from Scotland. This has the most simple of ingredients and is easy to make. He and both of his daughters said they taste like home. It is now a tradition for me to make these for them during the winter/snowboarding season.
Yum

OMG..something must have been left off this recipe. It is awful. I got a big handful of clumpy flour and was not moist at all. I could not roll it out it crumbles and I had to cut it with a biscuit cutter. Never again.

I've been using this recipe for years and it actually works perfectly as a cut-out cookie. I don't make any adjustments to the recipe itself - you can't go wrong with that simple but delicious butter+brown sugar flavor profile!
This was very tasty, despite being a non-traditional Scottish recipe. :)
